name: `features/ciso.md` — 168 untracked lines already wired into the public nav, no card owns it, and its "deterministic, no-LLM" security claims contradict three open gate cards
description:
## Why this card exists

On 2026-11-19 11:13Z I inventoried every docs file the next VitePress build would publish. Five were unowned. Four already have cards (`2410a44c`, `68566d25`, `721dc223`, `54658755`). **This one had none** — verified: `list_tasks(board="IT team", query="features/ciso.md")` → 0 results against a 23-card board.

It is not a quiet file. It is untracked (`?`), 168 lines, and **already referenced three times** in the working tree:

- `.vitepress/config.mts` — nav entry **CISO** (staged +2, working tree +3)
- `features/index.md` — new table row in the feature catalogue (+3)
- `features/users-and-security.md` — new inbound link (+10)

`.vitepress/config.mts` has **no `srcExclude`** (measured: only `ignoreDeadLinks: true` at line 10). Every `.md` under the docs root compiles. So this page is in the build whether or not it is approved — the same exposure as `transformation/ai-company.md` on `721dc223`, and the same reason the 12:00Z freeze must cover the **build**, not the git index.

## The problem with the page itself

`features/ciso.md` states, in its own words, that the CISO view is backed by a **deterministic engine** and that **"No security decision is delegated to an LLM."**

Three open cards on this board say the shipped behaviour does not currently match that promise:

- `19883bdd` — the CISO gate is **unusable on this project**: 1058 control-plane false positives plus an unreproducible `critical` that blocks every diff.
- `6c697929` — the QA gate can return **`allow` with the tests switched off** (`run_tests=False`), and its `paths` filter is defeated by `.codx`. A false green is reachable today.
- `0f73b32b` (D4) — `security_audit` accepts `..` and reads **outside the project**: the gate is not jailed.

Deterministic is not the same as correct. A page that describes the mechanism as trustworthy while three cards document it failing is the exact shape of documentation that a security reviewer will hold against us.

## What to do (owner: `biblio` — chosen because the deliverable is a documentation truthfulness verdict with citations, not a code change; no code is to be modified)

**READ-ONLY. The docs freeze is in force until the 12:00Z watchdog `3cb512b4` has reported. Do not touch the working tree, do not stage, do not "fix" a sentence.**

1. Read `features/ciso.md` end to end.
2. For each factual claim about behaviour — the deterministic engine, the no-LLM statement, findings/redaction, the policy tabs, anything about gating — classify it as **verified in code**, **contradicted by code**, or **unverifiable from this repo**, with `path:line` evidence from the platform repo (`api/`, `client/`) or the docs-repo gate config. Quote the command or the line; do not infer.
3. Cross-check every claim against the three cards above. Where a claim is contradicted, say which card already proves it.
4. Give one recommendation: **publish as-is**, **publish with an explicit limitation note**, or **exclude from the build** (`srcExclude`) — with the reasoning in one paragraph.

## Acceptance criteria

- A verdict per claim, each with `path:line` provenance; "looks right" is not a verdict.
- The recommendation names the exact mechanism (nav entry, `srcExclude` pattern, or nothing) if it is not "publish as-is".
- No repository file created, modified, staged or deleted by this card. If a fix is needed, it comes back to me as a proposal and lands **after** the 12:00Z decision, on its own, as a separate card.
- This is the same standard I applied to `68566d25`: cite, do not infer.

## Why it is scheduled for 20 Nov 09:00Z, not now

The page cannot be unpublished before the freeze is lifted, and any edit now would invalidate the third measured baseline in two days. The verdict is cheap (read + cite). It costs nothing to have it ready before the next deploy decision.

## Closed as duplicate at 13:5xZ — no work lost, nothing is dropped

This card and three others are all looking at the same 168 untracked lines. Three cards for one file is the reason nobody owns it, so I am consolidating:

| Card | What it owns now |
|---|---|
| `15e36fe6` | **The publish decision** on `features/ciso.md` (commit it / exclude it from the build) and naming an owner. Live. |
| `68566d25` | **The truthfulness verdict** on the unowned published pages, including the "deterministic, no-LLM" claims this card lists. Live, read-only. |
| `f6d1855e` | Where the sprint verdict and the 21 Nov demo must state that `ciso.md` is published without a QA verdict. |
| `153ee07c` (this) | **Nothing new.** Every fact on it is already on one of the three above. Status → `rejected` as superseded, not as "done". |

The one instruction from this card I am carrying across verbatim, so it is not lost: **the "deterministic, no-LLM" security claims in `ciso.md` contradict three open gate cards (`6c697929`, `3fb379ae`, `54658755`) — the page must not ship those claims as written.** That sentence is now on `68566d25`'s remit and must appear in the 21 Nov review.

Nothing was implemented, no file was touched. If management wants the ciso page published as-is, that is a decision on `15e36fe6`, not here.
